mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic demand, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, S&P 500 forward returns tend to decline over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS > 5.5%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS increases by 200,000+ in a month, signaling a strong labor market, S&P 500 returns tend to rise over the next 5 trading days due to increased consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 1.5% monthly increase in INDPRO, indicating a surge in industrial production, tends to lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased economic output.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high INDPRO growth periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) increases by 1%+ in a month, signaling increased consumer spending, and concurrently HOUST (housing starts) rises by 5%+, indicating a strong housing market, S&P 500 returns tend to increase over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in CPIAUCSL (consumer price index) by 0.5%+ in a month, signaling decreased inflationary pressures, tends to lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 55% of instances with CPIAUCSL decline > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: the level of UNRATE (unemployment rate) is inversely related to S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as lower unemployment typically indicates a stronger economy.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.015 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns do not show a significant inverse relationship with UNRATE levels (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) and HOUST (housing starts) both increase by 1%+ in a month, signaling a broadening economic expansion, S&P 500 returns tend to rise over the next 60 trading days due to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.
